([[Blythewood, South Carolina]]) * [[Link Academy (Missouri)|Link Academy]]
([[Branson, Missouri]]) | college = [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] (2022–2023) | draftyear = 2023 | draftround = 2 | draftpick = 35 | draftteam = [[Boston Celtics]] | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Chicago Bulls]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]]; [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team2 = →[[Windy City Bulls]] | years3 = {{nbay|2025|end}} | team3 = [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] | years4 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team4 = →[[Iowa Wolves]] | years5 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team5 = [[Houston Rockets]] | highlights = * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2022]]) }} '''Julian Phillips''' (born November 5, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]]. ==Early life and high school== Phillips was born in [[Killeen, Texas]] and moved to [[Columbia, South Carolina]] in the third grade after his parents, who were serving in the U.S. Army, were stationed at [[Fort Jackson (South Carolina)|Fort Jackson]].{{Cite web |last=Wardlaw |first=Lee |date=June 25, 2020 |title=Blythewood junior Julian Phillips is No. 1 basketball recruit in state for 2022 |url=https://www.coladaily.com/communities/blythewood/blythewood-junior-julian-phillips-is-no-1-basketball-recruit-in-state-for-2022/article_1136792a-b4bf-11ea-be96-b76380b3a420.html |access-date=January 18, 2023 |website=ColaDaily.com}} He initially attended Blythewood High School in [[Blythewood, South Carolina]]. Phillips transferred to Link Prep in [[Branson, Missouri]] after his junior year.{{Cite web |last=Bezjak |first=Lou |date=August 6, 2021 |title=Basketball recruit Julian Phillips to transfer to Link Year |url=https://www.thestate.com/sports/high-school/prep-basketball/article253295328.html |access-date=January 17, 2023 |website=[[The State (newspaper)|The State]]}} He played in the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during his senior year.{{Cite web |date=January 25, 2022 |title=LSU basketball signee Julian Phillips named to McDonald's All-American team |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/lsu-basketball-signee-julian-phillips-named-to-mcdonalds-all-american-team/article_9b9f1008-7e27-11ec-9cef-a76362092b32.html |access-date=January 17, 2023 |website=The Advocate}} Phillips was a consensus five-star recruit and one of the top 20 players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services.{{Cite web |last=Alvarez |first=Nick |date=May 12, 2022 |title=Auburn basketball misses on 5-star wing Julian Phillips |url=https://www.al.com/auburnbasketball/2022/05/auburn-basketball-misses-on-5-star-wing-julian-phillips.html |access-date=January 18, 2023 |website=[[AL.com]]}} He originally committed to play college basketball at [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] over offers from [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] and [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]] at the beginning of his senior season and signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] (NLI) during the early signing period.{{Cite web |last=Cobb |first=David |date=October 8, 2021 |title=LSU basketball recruiting: Five-star PF Julian Phillips, the No. 15 recruit in 2022 class, commits to Tigers |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/lsu-basketball-recruiting-five-star-pf-julian-phillips-the-no-15-recruit-in-2022-class-commits-to-tigers/ |access-date=January 17, 2023 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}}{{Cite web |date=November 10, 2021 |title=LSU basketball signs highly rated recruit Julian Phillips |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-branson-missouri-will-wade-basketball-5caa9b69ae164c61d5e761527964b7d6 |access-date=January 18, 2023 |publisher=[[Associated Press]]}} After LSU head coach [[Will Wade]] was fired, Phillips requested and was granted a release from his NLI and reopened his recruitment.{{Cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=March 18, 2022 |title=Julian Phillips, ESPN's No. 11 college basketball prospect, released from commitment to attend LSU |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33537750 |access-date=January 17, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} He ultimately committed to play at Tennessee after considering offers from [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]] and [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]].{{Cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=May 12, 2022 |title=Julian Phillips, final uncommitted five-star recruit in 2022 class, chooses to play at Tennessee |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33905002 |access-date=January 17, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} Phillips also considered playing professionally in the [[NBA G League]].{{Cite web |date=May 12, 2022 |title=Five-star SF Julian Phillips commits to Tennessee over Auburn, USC and G League Ignite |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4177142/2022/05/12/five-star-sf-julian-phillips-commits-to-tennessee-over-auburn-usc-and-g-league-ignite/ |access-date=January 18, 2023 |website=[[The Athletic]]}} ==College career== Phillips entered his freshman season at Tennessee as the Volunteers' starting [[small forward]].{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Toyloy III |date=December 8, 2022 |title=Why Tennessee's Julian Phillips is nation's most effective freshman |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2022/12/08/julian-phillips-stats-tennessee-basketball-rick-barnes/69710758007/ |access-date=January 18, 2023 |website=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]}} He was named to the 2022 [[Battle 4 Atlantis]] All-Tournament team after averaging a team-leading 13.3 points per game.{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Noah |date=November 25, 2022 |title=Tennessee beats Kansas, wins Battle 4 Atlantis finale |url=https://tennessee.rivals.com/news/tennessee-beats-kansas-wins-battle-4-atlantis-finale |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221126024407/https://tennessee.rivals.com/news/tennessee-beats-kansas-wins-battle-4-atlantis-finale |archive-date=November 26, 2022 |access-date=January 18, 2023 |website=[[Rivals.com]]}} Phillips played in 32 games with 25 starts as a freshman and averaged 8.3 points and 4.7 rebounds per game.{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Mike |date=March 24, 2023 |title=What Julian Phillips said about NBA Draft, future after Tennessee basketball loss |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2023/03/24/julian-phillips-tennessee-basketball-nba-draft-future-florida-atlantic/70018609007/ |access-date=April 28, 2023 |website=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]}} After the season, Phillips declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]] while maintaining his eligibility.{{Cite web |date=April 20, 2023 |title=Tennessee's Josiah-Jordan James and Julian Phillips will go through NBA Draft process |url=https://www.wbir.com/article/sports/college/vols/tennessees-josiah-jordan-james-julian-phillips-nba-draft-process/51-e2def424-88bd-41c6-a32d-c34b2b990086 |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=WBIR.com}} After taking part in the [[NBA draft combine]] and receiving positive feedback, he decided to remain in the draft.{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Mike |date=May 31, 2023 |title=Tennessee basketball's Julian Phillips to remain in NBA Draft |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2023/05/31/julian-phillips-nba-draft-tennessee-basketball/70275088007/ |access-date=June 20, 2023 |website=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]}} ==Professional career== === Chicago Bulls (2023–2026) === Phillips was selected with the 35th overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]], and was soon traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] via the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite web |date=June 22, 2023 |title=Kristaps Porzingis to Celtics, Marcus Smart to Grizzlies in 3-team deal |url=https://www.nba.com/news/kristaps-porzingis-trade-celtics-3-team-deal |access-date=June 23, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}{{Cite news |last=Glassbrook |first=Harvey |date=June 23, 2023 |title=Chicago Bulls trade into the draft and select Julian Phillips with the 35th pick |url=https://www.si.com/nba/bulls/news/chicago-bulls-trade-into-the-draft-and-select-julian-phillips-with-the-35th-pick |access-date=July 12, 2023 |work=Sports Illustrated}} Phillips made 40 appearances for the Bulls during his rookie campaign, recording averages of 2.2 points, 0.9 rebounds, and 0.3 assists.{{Cite web|title=Julian Phillips 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/5105553/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=April 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Phillips played in 79 contests (including five starts) for Chicago in the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 4.6 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 0.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Julian Phillips 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/5105553/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=April 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} He made 35 appearances (two starts) for Chicago during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], logging averages of 2.8 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 0.2 assists.{{Cite web|title=Julian Phillips 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/5105553/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=April 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} === Minnesota Timberwolves (2026) === On February 4, 2026, Philips and [[Ayo Dosunmu]] were traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in exchange for [[Rob Dillingham]], [[Leonard Miller (basketball)|Leonard Miller]], and four second-round picks.{{Cite web |title=Bulls continue demolition of roster, trade Ayo Dosunmu and others|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls/2026/02/05/bulls-continue-demolition-trading-ayo-dosunmu-and-others |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |language=en-US }}{{Cite web |title=Timberwolves acquire Ayo Dosunmu from Bulls in trade |url=https://www.nba.com/news/ayo-dosunumu-trade-wolves-bulls |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=[[NBA.com]] |language=en-US }} === Houston Rockets (2026–present) === On July 25, 2026, Phillips signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web |title=Rockets Sign Free Agent Julian Phillips {{!}} Houston Rockets |url=https://rockets.com/news/rockets-sign-free-agent-julian-phillips
